system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: Five failed logons for leo.martins occurred on WS-LMARTINS-01 between 13:30:32 and 13:30:56 UTC. They were LogonType 2 attempts through winlogon.exe, and the substatus indicates an incorrect password.
A successful Kerberos network logon for leo.martins was recorded on WS-NBLAKE-01 at 13:53:41 UTC, with source IP 10.40.10.23. The record does not identify the person or device behind that address.
At 13:57 UTC, Chrome traffic from WS-LMARTINS-01 reached the configured proxy and the proxy recorded a successful CONNECT tunnel to www.bing.com:443.

Several applications, including Zscaler, Cisco AnyConnect, Dropbox, OneDrive, Chrome, cmd.exe, and Explorer, terminated in a short interval around 14:07 UTC. The process-exit records establish that these processes ended, not why they ended.

The clustered application exits are followed by a logoff record for leo.martins at 14:07:16 UTC, making a session teardown a plausible explanation; the records do not establish that it was the cause of every process exit.

Dropbox and Cisco AnyConnect processes were running on WS-LMARTINS-01 before they terminated. The supplied environment context says Dropbox and VPN services are not approved, but these records do not show that either application was used for file transfer or remote access.
Proxy-related registry changes were recorded: MigrateProxy was set to 1 at 14:04, and ProxyEnable was set to 0 at 14:16.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied sensor-coverage status reports that DC-NWD-01 winsec and sysmon logs were not collected from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC because of a collection outage.
The supplied sensor-coverage status reports that FILE-NWD-01 winsec and sysmon logs were not collected from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC because of a collection outage.
The available workstation records do not include process-creation or command-line evidence explaining the failed logons, application exits, or proxy-setting changes.
claims_not_established: Whether the failed local logons were mistyped credentials or deliberate password guessing.
Who or what device initiated the successful network logon to WS-NBLAKE-01, and whether it was authorized.
Whether Dropbox or AnyConnect transferred data or provided remote access.
Whether the proxy-setting changes were authorized, caused by normal configuration activity, or intended to bypass monitoring.
Whether any related authentication, scheduled-job, or other activity occurred on DC-NWD-01 or FILE-NWD-01 during the collection outage.
additional_evidence_needed: Recover or obtain domain-controller authentication and account-management logs for 13:20–14:20 UTC, including relevant Kerberos and logon events.
Obtain FILE-NWD-01 authentication and process telemetry for the same window, including evidence about the svc-render password rotation and RenderQueue update.
Map 10.40.10.23 to a device using DHCP, asset, or network records and verify the reason for the network logon to WS-NBLAKE-01.
Review WS-LMARTINS-01 process-creation, command-line, session, and endpoint-protection telemetry around the failed logons, process exits, and proxy changes.

Review proxy and network-flow records for connections associated with Dropbox, AnyConnect, or other unapproved services, and confirm with the user or IT whether the software and configuration changes were authorized.
